chunks: 108 - The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “Jibrīl, peace be upon him, continued to counsel me regarding the siwak until I feared that I might wear down [my teeth] or make them fall out. And he continued to counsel me regarding the neighbor until I thought that he would make him an heir. And he continued to counsel me regarding the owned servant until I thought that he would set for him a fixed term in which he would be freed.”
And in another report: “And he continued to counsel me regarding the woman until I thought that her divorce should not be appropriate.”

key_terms.بِالْجَارِ: the neighbor; one whose rights and regard are emphasized
key_terms.بِالْمَرْأَةِ: the woman; referring here to concern for women’s treatment and rights
key_terms.بِالْمَمْلُوكِ: the owned servant; a bondservant whose treatment is addressed

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the importance of siwak, neighbors, servants, and women?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the repeated counsel of Jibrīl عليه السلام to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله regarding the siwak, the neighbor, the servant, and women. It highlights the great importance of personal cleanliness and the rights of others in social and family life, to the point that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله expected further legal consequence from that repeated emphasis.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.108 - The Messenger of Allah (sw) said:
"Archangel Jibril (as) kept advising me about the miswak until I feared I might wear down my teeth or make them fall out.
And Archangel Jibril (as) continued to advise me about the neighbor until I thought he would make him an heir.
And Archangel Jibril (as) continued to advise me about servants until I thought he would set a term for them to be freed."
In another report, "And Archangel Jibril (as) continued to advise me about women until I thought that divorce would not be appropriate for them."
